title: Creating mobile browser games with $0 budget on a work PC — Need feedback on my stack & tool recommendations!
author: KeismeyStudio
selftext:
Hi everyone!

I’m using AI to build small mobile browser games in my free time, but I’m working under a few constraints:

* **$0 budget** (or close to it)
* **No external software installation allowed** since I’m on a work PC, and some sites are blocked by my company's proxy.
* **100% free games: no ads, no microtransactions.**

**My current stack:**

* **Claude** (Pro subscription)
* **Gemini** (Free tier)
* **GitHub** (Free tier)
* **Cloudflare** (Free tier)

I have zero coding or art background, but I’m passionate about bringing my ideas to life.

Do you have any tips on how to optimize this setup, or any generous, browser-based free tools you’d recommend for assets, audio, or workflow?

If you’d like to check out what I’ve built so far with this setup, feel free to take a look here:[https://keismey.github.io/](https://keismey.github.io/)*(feedback is always welcome!)*

Thanks in advance for your help!

replies.author: KeismeyStudio
replies.body: On est d'accord, actuellement je met en pause les nouveaux jeux pour travailler sur la qualité de ceux déjà sortis, mais les limites d'utilisation de Claude Pro freine un peu.

comments.author: alanbdee
comments.body: First and foremost. If you're doing it on your work PC. They can have a strong argument for owning that code. Anything you do has to be on your personal equipment.

replies.author: KeismeyStudio
replies.body: Mon travail et mon entreprise n'ont rien à voir avec ce domaine, peu de chance qu'ils mettent le nez dedans.

comments.author: Need300dollars
comments.body: You should add rewarding ads to gain something. If you do, I'm willing to cooperate. Rev-share can be discussed. And while mobile browser game is fine, publishing in other platforms is more for marketing, at least Steam and Google Play Store. Well, AI can just make the controls for both, PC and Mobile, you can even focus the game as mobile and let PC be secundary development with not much thinking.

replies.author: KeismeyStudio
replies.body:
Mon envie de faire les jeux moi-même, en plus d'avoir des idées en tête, est venu d'une saturation des publicités sur les jeux mobiles, je ne veux pas faire ce que je déteste. 

Steam : 100$ pour publier, complètement hors budget.

PlayStore : La contrainte des 12 testeurs m'a complètement démotivé à poster dessus.

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body:
>on a work pc

Uh, don't do that. I'm telling you as an IT guy that's seen some shit. This can count as a breach of company policy (misuse of company assets), which can get you fired.

And everything you're doing on that computer is probably being logged in an easy to report manner.

replies.author: KeismeyStudio
replies.body: Mon travail et mon entreprise n'ont rien à voir avec ce domaine, peu de chance qu'ils mettent le nez dedans.

comments.author: Stinky_You
comments.body: ask claude after you have a good idea of what you're going to build in your game, claude can help make tools for itself and you to streamline the process a bit. my budget is limited to my claude sub.

comments.author: Fuzzzy420
comments.body:
What is it about fishing games? So many lately. 
For me fishing is boring in real life, why would I want a game about it?

replies.author: KeismeyStudio
replies.body: Haha, j'ai très peu pêché dans la vraie vie, mais j'adore la pêche dans les jeux. Je ne sais pas moi même pourquoi, mais j'adore ça, je pense que ça permet de casser le rythme du jeu et de profiter d'un instant tranquille.
